q1_issues.issue: "He" has no antecedent, so the witness must be classed person (and stemmed sk_person_1); classing it man reads the referent's kind off grammatical gender, which the instruction set explicitly forbids.
"Gareccio" is the bare, prepositionless direct object of "preached" yet is emitted as a Location on the event, a role the oblique rules license only for a PP that answers where.
Two Location atoms are stacked on one event, whereas the stacked-place rule puts the containing place on the inner place — (LocatedIn gareccio italy) — instead of a second event Location.
The relative clause "where he preached" yields no eventuality of its own; it is folded into sk_preach_1, so the second preaching predication is not recorded anywhere.

q2_gaps: Finite locative relative clause ("in Italy where he preached"): the instruction set covers reduced/participial relatives and uses relative clauses inside rule premises, but never states how a where-relativizer maps onto the Location role of the relative clause's own event.

A prepositionless place-name object of an otherwise intransitive verb ("preached Gareccio"): the role rules assume either an ordinary participant object decided by the change-of-state test or a PP decided by the question it answers, and cover neither reading of this string.
notes: The spend/exile half is well-formed — Possession for "his exile", Location for "in France", Past on the event, one Name per proper noun. The second half of the source sentence is garbled, which explains but does not license the Location-for-object choice.
